messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Me respondió No soy hombre y hombre ya fui, y mis padres fueron lombardos, mantuanos por patria ambos.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Rispuosemi: | “He answered me” – speaker performed the act of answering, directed to *me* | Me respondió | “He answered me” | OK | | Non | Negation particle; denies the predicate “man” | No | “Not / No” | OK | | omo (1) | Predicate nominal (negated): the speaker is **not** a man (present) | hombre | “man” | OK | | omo (2) | Predicate nominal (affirmed): the speaker **was** a man (past) | hombre | “man” | OK | | già | Temporal adverb indicating past time (“once”) | ya | “already / once” | OK | | fui | Copular verb, 1st sg. past historic: speaker existed as a man | fui | “I was” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction linking clauses | y | “and” | OK | | li | Definite article, masculine plural, marking *parenti* as specific | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | parenti | Noun, masculine plural: the speaker’s parents | padres | “parents” | OK | | miei | Possessive adjective, masculine plural: belonging to the speaker | mis | “my” | OK | | furon | Copular verb, 3rd pl. past historic: the parents **were** | fueron | “were” | OK | | lombardi | Predicate nominal (plural): ethnic identity “Lombards” | lombardos | “Lombards” | OK | | mantoani | Predicate nominal (plural): belonging to Mantua | mantuanos | “Mantuan(s)” | OK | | per | Preposition introducing the basis of identification | por | “by / for” | OK | | patrïa | Noun, feminine singular: “country” (criterion of identity) | patria | “country” | OK | | ambedui | Quantifier/pronoun meaning “both” (applies to speaker & parents) | ambos | “both” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *li* – the definite article is not required in Spanish and was omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected in the alignment (the Spanish rendering follows the source meaning and respects target‑language syntax).

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
